correctness.rationale: For a nonzero \(F\)-linear map \(t:E\to E\) on a quadratic field extension, rank two makes \(t\) surjective and the trace-algebra axiom forces multiplication by \(t(1)\). Rank one gives image \(Fz\); applying the axiom at a nonzero image element forces \(z\in F^\times\), so the map is an arbitrary nonzero functional \(E\to F\). Conversely every such functional satisfies the axiom. In a purely inseparable quadratic extension the field trace is zero, so these functionals are not \(x\mapsto\operatorname{Tr}(cx)\). The explicit \(F_2(s)\subset F_2(s)(u)\), \(u^2=s\), example checks directly.

originality.rationale: The complete primary preprint arXiv:2609.19797v1 was inspected. Its Lemma 7 explicitly asserts that every rank-one trace has form \(\operatorname{Tr}_{E/F}(cx)\) over an arbitrary field, and its proof divides by a trace quantity that vanishes in the inseparable case; Proposition 11 repeats the resulting incomplete family. Targeted searches found no correction predating this 2026-09-18 record. A near-identical SCOPE correction exists on 2026-09-19, which postdates the audited record.

value.rationale: The claim repairs a false advertised arbitrary-field classification, gives an exhaustive replacement family, and isolates separability as the exact missing hypothesis while leaving the finite-field results intact. Correcting a classification theorem with a concrete family of counterexamples is a substantive mathematical contribution.

limitations: The correction concerns the arbitrary-field quadratic-extension classification. The classical separability criterion is not new, and finite-field results of the source remain unaffected because finite fields are perfect. The source preprint may later be revised.
